cards.text: The exiles are back from Babylon, sent home by a proclamation from Cyrus, king of Persia, to rebuild the house of the LORD (Ezra 1:1-3). By the seventh month they've settled in their towns, and the people gather “as one man” in Jerusalem. A whole crowd moving like ONE guy, friend, and the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with couldn't even agree on who had the most charge left!

Two leaders step up: Jeshua son of Jozadak, a priest, with his fellow priests, and Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, who came back with the exiles (Ezra 2:2), with his associates. They're ready to sacrifice burnt offerings to the God of Israel, just like it's written in the Law of Moses.

cards.question: Jeshua and Zerubbabel are ready to offer burnt offerings to the God of Israel. So what do they start building first?

cards.text: They set the altar up on its foundation, and the burnt offerings to the LORD begin, morning and evening. But something is hanging over all of it.

cards.question: The Israelites keep the morning and evening burnt offerings going, even though they ___ the people of the land.

cards.text: They also celebrate a feast, just like it's written in the Law. And friend, when it's feast time, you do NOT hit snooze!

cards.question: In the seventh month, the Israelites back in Jerusalem celebrate a feast just like it's written. Which feast is it?
During the Feast of Tabernacles, the Israelites offer burnt offerings every day, following the number prescribed for each day.

cards.text: After that, the altar gets a FULL schedule: the regular burnt offerings, the New Moons, all the appointed sacred feasts of the LORD, plus every freewill offering people bring. That altar's got a busier calendar than my ovens, and friend, my ovens are BUSY.

cards.question: When the Israelites start offering burnt offerings on the first day of the seventh month, the foundation of the temple of the LORD has already been laid.

cards.text: Then they get ready to build. They pay the masons and carpenters, and they send food, drink and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, cities on the coast, to bring cedar logs from Lebanon.

cards.question: The cedar logs from Lebanon make their way to Joppa by ___.
The Israelites arrange this whole cedar shipment on their own, without any go-ahead from Cyrus, king of Persia.

cards.text: In the second month of the second year after they arrived at the house of God in Jerusalem, the work begins. Zerubbabel, Jeshua, the priests, the Levites and everyone back from captivity: all hands on deck!

cards.question: The work on the house of the LORD needs supervisors. Who do Zerubbabel, Jeshua and their associates appoint?

answers.text: Levites twenty years old and up

cards.text: So Levite families team up to oversee the workers: Jeshua with his sons and brothers, Kadmiel and his sons, and the sons of Henadad, all of them Levites. Nothing makes you lay a stone straighter than a supervisor standing right behind you!
And then it happens: the builders lay the foundation of the temple of the LORD. A FOUNDATION, friend, an actual FOUNDATION!
The priests in their apparel take their positions with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, come with cymbals. They do it just the way David king of Israel had prescribed.

cards.question: At the new temple foundation, the priests with trumpets and the Levites with cymbals take their positions. What are they there to do?

cards.text: They sing back and forth with praise and thanksgiving to the LORD: “For He is good; for His loving devotion to Israel endures forever.”

cards.question: Then all the people give a great ___ of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD has been laid.

cards.text: Now listen close, friend. Not every sound in that crowd is a cheer.

cards.question: Some in the crowd weep loudly when they see the foundation of this temple. Who are they?

answers.text: Older leaders who saw the first temple
The people of Sidon and Tyre

cards.question: While those older leaders weep, many others in the crowd shout joyfully.
The crowd at the new temple foundation is making so much noise. What can't the people do?

answers.text: Tell the shouts of joy from the weeping
See the foundation through the crowd
Finish singing the song they started

cards.question: The sound of the crowd at the new temple foundation in Jerusalem is heard from far away.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set this batch down for now, friend. Only the foundation's in, and this story is FAR from done.
